title: Occlusion, outside-frame, and unknown are different
plainLanguage: If an elbow is behind the torso, that is different from the elbow being outside the picture or the program simply not knowing where it is.
purpose: Avoid invented joints and make hidden-part knowledge useful for later layer ordering and artwork decisions.

rules.statement: Use visible, occluded, out_of_frame, and unknown as distinct states.
A hidden part may be verified as hidden without inventing its coordinate.
Low detector confidence or transparency does not prove occlusion.
Repeated occlusion patterns should become searchable reference evidence for perspective and layer-order decisions.

implementation.currentSupport: Visibility states and hidden-without-coordinate verification exist. Corpus Pane 0.2.2.4 counts explicit hidden/out-of-frame anatomy as known regional coverage, excludes it from projected geometry, and treats hidden-versus-visible as a real retrieval mismatch rather than a perfect match.
implementation.futureWork: Use reviewed occlusion relationships to inform assembly layer-order tests.
